note: Adapted from the species-level description in Chhotani (1997), originally in English; alates, soldiers and workers are all described; synonymy, literature citations, figure numbers and distribution records are not translated; the numerical details of the wing-surface microstructure are omitted, and biological information is placed under Other.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule yellow to reddish brown, antennae, labrum and legs paler, mandibles black with reddish brown base, thorax and abdomen creamy yellow to pale rusty yellow. Pilosity of head and body moderate. Body length 6.5–9.0 mm. Head capsule subrectangular, longer than wide (head length to base of mandibles 2.25–3.10, maximum width 1.80–2.50 mm); widest posteriorly, the width exceeding 3/4 of the length; sides gradually narrowing anteriorly, sometimes almost parallel. Antennae 17-segmented; segment 3 shortest, segment 4 longer than segment 5. Boundary between postclypeus and frons indistinct; anteclypeus white, narrow, bare, band-like. Labrum ligulate, narrowing to a point anteriorly. Mandibles stout and powerful, sickle-shaped, slightly longer than half the head length (length 1.20–1.65 mm, mandible length/head length index 0.51–0.59). Left mandible with a medium-sized tooth near the middle (tooth index 0.50–0.55, the angle of the tooth varying from a right angle to slightly less than a right angle); right mandible with a small tooth at the basal third. Postmentum subrectangular, slightly inflated near the basal third (length 1.30–2.0, maximum width 0.73–0.93 mm). Pronotum saddle-shaped (length 0.75–1.00, width 1.40–1.83 mm), anterior margin with a weak median emargination, posterior margin weakly to deeply concave; posterior margins of meso- and metanotum nearly straight.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Workers dimorphic. Major worker: head capsule pale yellow to rusty yellow, antennae paler, thorax, abdomen and legs creamy yellow; pilosity of head moderate, body pilosity fairly dense. Body length 5.0–6.5 mm. Head capsule subquadrate, slightly wider than long; sides nearly parallel, widest at the antennal base (length to apex of labrum 2.05–2.50, to base of mandibles 1.50–1.85, maximum width 1.68–2.10 mm). Fontanelle plate small and round. Antennae 19-segmented, segments 3 and 4 subequal, segment 5 shortest. Postclypeus weakly inflated, length less than half the width, pilose; anteclypeus sub-trapezoidal, transparent, projecting forwards at the middle of the anterior margin. Labrum dome-shaped. Pronotum as in the soldier (length 0.48–0.65, width 0.85–1.20 mm). Minor worker: resembling the major worker but smaller (body length 3.5–4.70 mm, length to apex of labrum 1.70–2.0, to base of mandibles 1.10–1.48, maximum head width 1.15–1.50, pronotum length 0.35–0.53, width 0.58–0.90 mm).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule chestnut brown to dark reddish brown, postclypeus and legs rusty yellow, paler than the head capsule, antennae pale reddish brown, pronotum brown, paler than the head capsule, with a yellow T-shaped mark and shoulder spots, mesonotum paler than the pronotum, abdominal tergites brown, sternites pale yellow. Pilosity of head and pronotum moderate, abdominal pilosity dense. Body length (including wings) 24.0–25.5 mm, without wings 13.75–15.20 mm. Head capsule subcircular, distinctly wider than long (length to apex of labrum 2.95–3.40, to base of mandibles 1.65–2.20, width including compound eyes 2.65–2.90 mm). Fontanelle small, slightly raised above the head surface, situated at the middle of the dorsal midline. Compound eyes subcircular, medium-sized (maximum diameter 0.65–0.78, minimum diameter 0.58–0.78 mm). Ocelli oval, medium-sized (maximum diameter 0.30–0.38, minimum diameter 0.18–0.26 mm), separated from the compound eye by about their short diameter (0.18–0.26 mm). Antennae 19-segmented; segment 3 shorter than segment 2 or 4, subequal to segment 5. Postclypeus pilose, extremely inflated, length about equal to half the width. Anteclypeus sub-trapezoidal, projecting forwards at the middle of the anterior margin. Labrum subquadrate, pilose, setae longer near the anterior margin. Pronotum trapezoidal, narrower than the head; anterior margin slightly raised with a weak median emargination, posterior margin also weakly incurved at the middle (length 1.30–1.48, width 2.30–2.60 mm). Wings entirely pilose, especially at the margins, pale brown; media with 6–7 main branches on the wing, some of them forked again, cubitus with 8–10 main branches; fore wing length 21.0–23.0, hind wing length 19.5–21.0 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The species is of considerable economic importance, damaging houses and structural timber and acting as a pest of various crops, orchards and forest trees as well as of plantation crops such as tea and Eucalyptus. Nests are generally subterranean, although mound building has also been reported; Bose (1992b) reported the unusual behaviour of building mounds inside roofed sheds in Manipur. The swarming period is reported as June to November and varies with locality.
